sara_cs: Quick weekly health check for ACME-123 — variant uptake + fallback impact. TL;DR: rdx-v2-small now handles ~42% of token volume, fallback rate up to 12% (was 4% last week). P95 latency for v2-small is 280ms; account p95 ~350ms. Spend +18% WoW. Need to confirm whether fallbacks are due to quality regressions or runtime timeouts.

mike_data: dropping the numbers I pulled from analytics (last 7 days):
```
total_tokens: 38.2M
rdx-v2-small_tokens: 16.0M (41.9%)
fallbacks_total: 4.6M tokens (12.0% of v2-small requests)
rdx-v1-stable_receiving_fallbacks: 4.6M tokens
median_latency_p50: 110ms
p95_latency_v2-small: 280ms
p95_latency_account: 350ms
errors_rate_v2-small: 0.9% (timeouts + partial outputs)
weekly_spend_change: +18% vs prior week
```

devin_eng: noted. We pushed a kernel patch yesterday (13:22 PT) to reduce context switching latency in the runtime — could explain a small p95 shift. I also saw an oddness in the fallback gate: some requests hit a policy that prefers v1-stable when token burn estimate > threshold, and the estimator occasionally overestimates for long prompts. Investigating. @mike_data can you surface sample request_ids for fallbacks?

tina_support: FYI — 3 support tickets opened this week referencing slow responses and truncated outputs, all flagged with rdx-v2-small. I asked the customer for the offending prompts and examples; they replied this morning and attached 6 examples. I uploaded them to the shared drive.

ops-bot: deploy: rdx-runtime v1.12.3 applied on host pool-3 (deploy id dpl-8791) at 2026-02-28T13:22:10Z :white_check_mark:

mike_data: breakdown by route (7d): chat routes -> fallback 18%, generation-only routes -> 7%, embeddings -> 0.2%. Most fallbacks concentrated in chat@/conversational_long. Also correlation with sequences > 1024 tokens.

devin_eng: thanks. that matches the estimator theory — long chat sequences trigger overestimate. Short-term mitigation: lower the token-estimate threshold for the account and enable conservative fallback gating for canary — will push a config change this afternoon. Longer-term: improve estimator via sampling.

sara_cs: action items:
- @devin_eng apply conservative gating for ACME-123 by EOD (reduce auto-fallback threshold).
- @mike_data share request_ids + a CSV of top 50 fallbacks and the 6 customer examples (sensitive redacted).
- @tina_support follow up with ACME and offer a short enablement session to walk prompt patterns and recommend prompt-engineering for v2-small.
- eng + cs to meet tomorrow 11:00 PT for 20m sync to confirm metrics after gating.

Can folks ack and add anything I missed? :eyes:
